Below is a one‐line patch to prevent the JSDoc rule from greedily matching an empty `/**/` comment. In essence we tighten its “begin” regex so that it will no longer fire when the next character after the `**` is a `/`. Empty block comments will now fall back to the normal C‐style comment mode and highlighting will continue correctly.

Explanation of the change:

- Original begin‐pattern: `'/\*\*'`  
  This matches `/**` even if immediately followed by `/` (i.e. `/**/`).

- New begin‐pattern: `'/\*\*(?!\/)'`  
  The `(?!\/)` look‐ahead ensures we do **not** match when the very next character is a `/`, so an empty `/**/` falls through to the generic C‐style comment matcher (`hljs.C_BLOCK_COMMENT_MODE`) and does not confuse the JSDoc matcher.  
  This restores correct highlighting for the rest of the line after an empty block comment.
